title: Choose the sound delegation
scenario: Your landlord kept part of your deposit and sent a letter explaining why. You want AI help responding — and you are deciding what to actually ask it for.
task: Pick the request that delegates the right things to AI.
promptA: Here is my landlord's letter about the deposit. Am I legally right to get the full amount back? Answer yes or no, and write the final reply I should send.
promptB: Here is my landlord's letter about the deposit. (1) Summarize it in three points. (2) List what I should verify under the tenancy rules. (3) Draft a neutral request for the remainder, for my review — and flag anything that reads as legal advice so I check it with a tenancy advisor.

feedback.a: Asking for a legal verdict and a final reply delegates the two things that must stay human: the judgment and the accountability. A confident yes-or-no is exactly the wrong output shape for a real consequence.
feedback.b: It uses AI for what it does well — compressing the letter, listing what to check, drafting for review — and routes the legal judgment to the advisor and the decision to you.

hints: Which request treats the model as an assistant, and which treats it as a lawyer?
After each reply is sent: who is accountable if it is wrong?
explanation: The three-tier rule decides it: drafting and summarizing sit in 'delegate or assist', a legal verdict sits in 'keep human'. Prompt B keeps the material-production on the AI side and the consequence-bearing judgment where a professional can own it — with flags so advice-shaped output gets caught before it is acted on.
